findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` as a parameter but passes the outer-scope `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the dashboard-widget split path, `_get_event_stats` is intentionally called with a different dataset (e.g. `discover` for the errors-only query, or `split_dataset`), so the eligibility decision will be computed for the wrong dataset. Consequence: count() can be rewritten to `upsampled_count()` for a transactions-like query (where `sample_weight` is not meaningful/absent), or conversely skipped for a genuine errors query, producing wrong numbers or Snuba errors.

findings.title: Caching option-based allowlist in shared cache creates stale/incorrect results and cross-test pollution
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist eligibility in the global cache for 60s, keyed by org id and `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Problems: (1) the option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` change takes up to 60s to take effect, and the only invalidation helper (`invalidate_upsampling_cache`) is never called anywhere, so there is no real invalidation path; (2) `hash()` of a tuple is not a stable or collision-free key — different project sets can collide, giving a wrong eligibility answer for an unrelated project list; (3) the docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` claims the config is read fresh every time, which the cache contradicts. Also the option lookup is already cheap/cached in Sentry, so the cache adds risk for no real gain. This also makes the new endpoint tests order-dependent/flaky, since tests mocking different allowlists for the same org+project set share the cache entry.

findings.title: Cached value type not validated; truthy-return instead of bool
findings.body: `cached_result` is returned as `cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(...)`, which returns the cached object (not a bool) when it is falsy — e.g. returns `False`/`0` from the cache but with declared return type `bool`. More importantly the function is typed `-> bool` while potentially returning a non-bool cache payload. Callers compare it truthily today, but any `is True` check or typed consumer would break.

findings.title: upsampled_count relies on `sample_weight` column existing in discover/errors tables
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction aggregates `sum(sample_weight)` with no guard. If the underlying Snuba table (discover/errors) does not have a `sample_weight` column, or it is NULL for non-sampled events, queries will either fail with a Snuba error or return 0/NULL counts for allowlisted projects. The code comment asserts the schema guarantees this, but nothing in this PR enforces it (the only place setting sampling data is the test factory, which writes `sample_rate`, not `sample_weight`). Consider a fallback such as `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` and declaring `default_result_type="integer"` to match the `toInt64` result.

findings.title: Error-focused query detection by substring is unreliable
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring check for `event.type:error` on the lowercased query string. This matches negated filters like `!event.type:error` and free-text/message content containing that string, and misses equivalent forms (`event.type:[error, default]`, `event.type: error`). For the discover dataset that means count() can be silently rewritten to `upsampled_count()` on queries that explicitly exclude errors, returning inflated counts. Use the parsed search query/filters instead of a substring match.

findings.title: Unused `organization` parameter and dead invalidation helper
findings.body: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` takes `organization` but never uses it, and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called from anywhere in the codebase, so the cache added in this PR has no invalidation path. Either wire the invalidation into the option-change path or drop both.

findings.title: Blanket `except Exception: pass` silently drops invalid sample rates in test factory
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps both the context read and the float conversion in bare `except Exception: pass`. A malformed `client_sample_rate` (e.g. a string, or contexts not being a dict) will silently leave `sample_rate` unset, making upsampling tests pass with regular counts and masking real bugs. At minimum narrow the exceptions (`AttributeError`/`TypeError`/`ValueError`) and/or assert in tests.

findings.title: Accidental git submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed
findings.body: The PR adds a gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This is clearly an accidental nested clone of the repository itself; it will break `git submodule` operations and clones for other developers/CI. Remove it before merge.

findings.title: New endpoint tests mock `options` module-wide but do not clear the upsampling cache
findings.body: These tests patch `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options`, but `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches eligibility in the shared cache for 60s under a key derived from org id + project ids. Because all tests in the class use the same org and project pair, whichever test runs first seeds the cache and the subsequent tests (partial allowlist, no allowlist) can read the stale eligibility value, making the assertions order-dependent and flaky. The tests need to flush the cache in `setUp`, or the caching should be removed.

findings.title: Duplicated upsampling transform logic invites divergence
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is invoked in three separate branches (top_events, use_rpc, default) guarded by the same `upsampling_enabled` flag, each re-deriving `final_columns` from `query_columns`. The `should_upsample`/`upsampling_enabled` aliasing adds no value. Computing `final_columns` once right after the eligibility check would remove the risk of a future branch forgetting the transform.
